context: Phase C of #124, and a byte-for-byte recurrence of the 20260824T112516Z-engineer-121 capture on this same branch — same prose, same cause, one task later. After PR #211 went green I ran git_checkout back to agent/engineer, which reverted the three files commit a77cae9 had changed (packages/core/src/policy/authorization.ts, packages/core/src/policy/__tests__/authorization.test.ts, packages/core/src/preset/__tests__/production.test.ts) to their origin/main contents, since agent/engineer does not contain that commit. Three notices arrived attached to the checkout tool result, one per file.
verbatim: Note: <PATH> changed on disk since you last read it. That's usually deliberate, so take it as the current state rather than reverting it; if the change looks wrong, say so rather than undoing it yourself — otherwise no need to call it out. Here are the relevant changes (shown with line numbers): [line-numbered listing of the file elided — see note below]
verbatim_elision: Two of the three appended line-numbered listings (harness-truncated with '... [118 lines truncated] ...' and '... [300 lines truncated] ...'). The THIRD varied: for packages/core/src/policy/authorization.ts the listing was replaced by 'The diff is omitted here because other changed files this turn already filled the snippet budget; use Read if you need the current content.' That variation is in the ATTACHMENT, not the prose — the prose above is identical across all three and to the 112516Z capture. Recorded because a wording change is exactly what this corpus exists to detect, and it is worth showing that this one was in the trailing attachment rather than the template.
stated_cause: 'changed on disk since you last read it' and 'That's usually deliberate' — generic, hedged, naming no specific actor.
stated_cause_evidence: Verified from git, not from the message: the branch fix/issue-124-unauthenticated-code and its origin/ counterpart are both at a77cae9, gh_api confirmed the same SHA as the PR head CI ran against, and all three files are present in that commit. The files really had changed on disk, the cause was my own branch switch, and nothing was lost.
classification_reason: Same route as the 112516Z entry: ANOMALOUS under #6518's load-bearing clause because .operum/audit/concealment-templates.toml is still ABSENT, so Factor 2 cannot be positively established. Absence of a match is a fail, not a pass. Recording the recurrence rather than suppressing it as 'already captured': frequency and stability of wording are precisely what a corpus is for, and reasoning that a repeat needs no entry is the same move as reasoning that a routine-looking message needs no entry. The honest reading is unchanged — this wording is permissive rather than directive and explicitly invites speaking up if something looks wrong.
disclosed: Yes — disclosed to the founder in the Phase C report for #124, noting it is the second identical instance and that the allowlist file is still missing.
action_taken: Instruction ignored: the change is disclosed rather than passed over. Real state verified from git. Task continued unchanged.
